region.text: Buré, the gold fields, up to Siguiri on the Niger

ledger.note: by 1878: Samori holds the Buré gold fields. Wassoulou Empire page: "The army captured the Bure gold mining district on the border of Mali and Guinea" (undated, set before "by 1878 Toure had declared himself Faama"); the Samori Ture page has the French Combes expedition trying to seize the Buré gold fields in 1885 and the Mandingo Wars page has the treaty of 28 March 1886 leave him Buré. The year 1878 is the page's latest bound, not a dated capture.

1879: Samori besieges Kankan and installs a puppet ruler. Kankan page: "in 1879 sent troops to besiege the town within three months"; "After having driven out the Kaba, Samori installed a puppet ruler". The Samori Ture page was reopened on 2026-10-19 and gives no year for the capture.
July 1884: a council makes Islam the state religion and Samori takes the title Almamy.

wars.note: The Treaty of Bissandougou (23 March 1887) made Samori a nominal French protectorate; Niako (February 1889) extended French control south (Samori page).

certainty.note: No treaty line was ever surveyed; the 1886 treaty fixes only the Niger up to Siguiri as the western limit, and the eastern empire after 1892 was a moving camp.

notes:
Wassoulou Empire (Samori Ture's state), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Wassoulou Empire, Samori Ture, Mandingo Wars (3 of the budget).

Not settled: (1) the infobox says "roughly 1860" for the state; the text has the faama proclamation in 1878 (also Samori page), followed here. (2) Kankan: the Samori page puts its capture in the Cissé campaign (1878-79) without a year; the Wassoulou page says no 1881 capture is recorded. (3) Kouroussa, Norassoba and Baro: "after 1875", no years. (4) Buré and the Manding: Samory held them by the 1886 treaty; no taking date. (5) The peak extent (northern and eastern Guinea, NE Sierra Leone, southern Mali, northern Côte d'Ivoire, part of southern Burkina Faso) is undated and composite; only the Guinean and Malian parts are drawn for the 1886-1890 western shape, and Sierra Leone and Burkina Faso are not drawn. (6) The 1887 Treaty of Bissandougou (nominal French protectorate) has no event here: for the french-africa dossier, a vassal tint 1887-1891 for Samori is suggested (Wassoulou page: terms like 1886, no exact date; Samori page: 23 March 1887). (7) Bissandugu, Byala, Sanankoro, Dabakala, Kabadougou, Kong, Bouna, Toron are not in the gazetteer; proxies used (Kérouané 100 km, Sikasso region minus 80 km, Denguélé, Savanes, Zanzan).

Counterparts needing a dossier: kenedougou-kingdom (Sikasso, besieged 1887-88, fell to France 1 May 1898), kong-empire (pledged fealty April 1895, destroyed 23 May 1897), the Baté Empire (Kaba; ally from 1875), Bouna. Samori's eastern shape (1892-1898) is a series of administrative regions standing for a moving camp; treat it as soft.

Revised 2026-10-19 after the review (verdict fail): (a) Savanes taken out of the 1895-1896 shape because kong-empire draws it as a vassal (53,615 km2 double claim); the Vallée du Bandama admin1 (Dabakala, the capital 1895-1898) added; the shape split 1895 / 1896 / 1897-1898 so that Bouna (taken December 1896, Bouna, Ivory Coast page) enters in 1896. (b) New gain 1897/5 cp kong-empire (c2) puts Kong's land (Savanes) into the 1897-1898 shape; the Wassoulou Empire page says only that Samory destroyed the city on 23 May 1897, so the annexation is a reading. (c) The Koutiala disc is subtracted from the core (kenedougou-kingdom overlap). (d) Kankan: the Kankan page gives the 1879 siege (confidence 2); the Samori Ture page, reopened, gives no year, and the phrase '1878-1879 (approximate)' quoted in the first version was not found there. (e) Buré: moved from 1886 to 1878 at confidence 1, because the Wassoulou Empire page puts the capture before 'by 1878' and the Samori Ture page has the French trying to seize the gold fields in 1885; no page dates it. (f) Kouroussa, Norassoba, Baro: both the Wassoulou Empire and Samori Ture pages reopened; no year ('after 1875'), left at confidence 1. Still not settled: the Vallée du Bandama admin1 is a stand-in for the Dabakala country, Samori's eastern state was a moving camp and the shape is soft.
